problem: VLN agents on R2R plug in out-of-domain pre-trained representations (GloVe word embeddings, ImageNet ResNet features) and must bridge the domain gap while also learning to act. With only 7,189 human-annotated instruction-path pairs, fine-tuning on navigation alone adapts these representations poorly. Speaker-generated augmented data (Fried et al.) is also noisy, and there was no way to rank its quality.
motivation: Human instructions are specific to the paths they describe, so incorrect instruction-path pairs can be mined cheaply from the environment without any new annotation. Discriminative in-domain auxiliary tasks trained before agent training can therefore adapt the language and visual encoders. The agent can then focus on learning to act rather than on aligning representations.
key_idea: Pre-train the agent's GloVe/bi-LSTM language encoder and panoramic LSTM visual encoder on two annotation-free tasks, then warm-start the navigation agent (RCM or Speaker-Follower) from these adapted encoders. The tasks are Cross-Modal Alignment (tell true instruction-path pairs from mined negative paths) and Next Visual Scene (CPC/InfoNCE prediction of future visual latents).
insight: The two auxiliary tasks are complementary. NVS alone hurts the agent (RCM val-unseen SPL 20.6 vs 32.7 without pre-training) because nothing trains cross-modal or language components. CMA alone helps (SPL 42.0), and CMA+NVS is best (SPL 43.0); NVS also raises CMA discrimination AUC on val-unseen from 72.0 to 79.2. Hard negatives matter: training only on easy Path-Substitution negatives gives 64.5 AUC (vs 72.0 with all three strategies) and no diagonal word-to-view alignment, since the model can shortcut on start/end locations. Warm-starting both encoders matters: val-unseen SPL is 43.0 with both, versus 35.8 with language only, 33.1 with image only and 32.7 with neither. Most of the gain comes from shorter, more efficient paths (PL 14.8→9.8 m), which improves SPL far more than SR.
method: Negative path mining: for each R2R instruction, keep the text and corrupt the path, giving 10 negatives per positive (4 PS, 3 RW, 3 PR). Path Substitution (PS) takes another path from the same house. Random Walk (RW) samples a same-length walk sharing the start or end node that ends/starts at least 5 m away. Partial Reordering (PR) keeps the endpoints fixed and shuffles the middle nodes.

Two-tower encoder: a 2-layer bi-LSTM (256 units per direction) over 300-d GloVe embeddings (vocab = tokens with ≥5 occurrences) for the instruction. A 2-layer LSTM (512 units) over attention-pooled 36-view panoramic features (pre-trained CNN features + [sinφ, cosφ, sinθ, cosθ]) for the path.

Cross-Modal Alignment (CMA): alignment matrix A = H^X (H^V)^T. Row-wise softmax-weighted pooling is followed by softmin-weighted pooling to produce a 'best worst-case alignment' scalar score, trained with cross-entropy to separate positive pairs from mined negatives.

Next Visual Scene (NVS): CPC-style InfoNCE loss that predicts the visual latents v_{t+k} (k=1,2) from the visual LSTM state h_t^V through a bilinear f=exp(v^T W_k h). Negatives come from the mined negative paths.
Joint objective α·L_alignment + (1−α)·L_coherence with α=0.5, optimized with Momentum at lr 1e-2 (decay 0.8 every 0.5M steps).

Transfer (ALTR): the language and visual encoders of a reimplemented RCM agent are warm-started from the jointly trained model (agent lr 1e-5). The agent is trained on R2R train plus Fried augmented data with behavior cloning interleaved with REINFORCE (distance-reduction reward plus a terminal success reward). The number K of BC batches per PG batch decays exponentially.
CMA scorer as data filter: the trained model ranks Fried's augmented instruction-path pairs. Training on the top-ranked 1%/2% beats training on the bottom-ranked 1%/2%.

setting.backbone: Reimplemented RCM agent (bi-LSTM language encoder with GloVe + LSTM visual encoder over pre-trained ImageNet CNN panoramic features), encoders warm-started from auxiliary-task pre-training; also a reimplemented Speaker-Follower agent
setting.training_data: Auxiliary pre-training uses R2R train paths as positives with 10 automatically mined negatives each (PS/RW/PR; no extra human annotation). Agent training uses R2R train plus the Speaker-Follower (Fried et al.) speaker-generated augmented data.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 discretized views, pre-trained CNN features + orientation features)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (choose among navigable directions)
setting.privileged: none (single trajectory, no beam search, no pre-exploration of test environments)

numbers_note: Path Length (PL) is mapped to TL. The paper also reports several non-navigation results, none of which are included above. Instruction-path discrimination AUC on the authors' own PR+RW-negative validation sets: CMA 82.6/72.0, NVS 63.0/62.1, CMA+NVS 84.0/79.2 (val seen / val unseen) in Table 3; a negative-sampling-strategy AUC ablation in Table 1. Table 2 reports an RCM agent trained on only the top/bottom 1% or 2% of Fried augmented data ranked by the CMA scorer (e.g., top-2% val-unseen SR 22.3 / SPL 18.5 vs bottom-2% 17.5 / 14.1). An encoder-transfer ablation appears in Table 6 (val-unseen SPL: image-only 33.1, language-only 35.8). R2R val numbers for their reimplemented baselines differ from the original papers: their reimplemented RCM gets val-seen SR 55.3 vs 67.6 reported by the original RCM.
results: On the R2R test leaderboard, ALTR (RCM warm-started from CMA+NVS representations) reaches SPL 45.0 / SR 48.0 / NE 5.49 / PL 10.3. This beats the prior best single-run, no-pre-exploration agents, the Regretful Agent (SPL 40.0) and RCM (SPL 38.0), by 5 SPL points while tying their SR of 48.0. On val-unseen, pre-training lifts the reimplemented RCM from SR 41.1 / SPL 32.7 to 46.1 / 43.0 and the Speaker-Follower from 36.0 / 29.0 to 40.0 / 31.2, mostly by producing shorter paths.
limitations: Auxiliary pre-training and agent training are separate stages rather than joint (the authors list joint training as future work), and NVS alone degrades navigation.

Evaluated only on R2R. The reimplemented baselines are notably weaker on val-seen than the originally published RCM/SF numbers, and test SR does not improve over the prior best (ties at 48.0); gains are mainly in SPL/path length.
Still relies on GloVe + frozen ImageNet CNN features and on the noisy speaker-augmented data. The quality ranking of augmented data is shown only in small 1–2% subsets.
